title: Convoy TAKA-206, 22–23 November 1944
eyebrow: East of Formosa · Coordinated attack group "Sandy's Sluggers", Cdr L. D. McGregor in REDFISH

participants.name: REDFISH
participants.co: Cdr L. D. McGregor, pack commander

participants.name: SHAD
participants.co: L. Julihn (middle initial illegible on the report)

paras.text: The three boats' torpedo attacks of 22–23 November 1944, as typed on their attack sheets, beside the log the convoy's minesweeper W-15 kept of the same night. Times are converted to GMT, so BANG and SHAD (zone K) and the Japanese escorts (zone I) share one clock.

Three of the six ships were sunk (Hozan, Amakusa and Sakae Maru); Taiken, Sannin and Eikai Maru sheltered at Funauki (W-15's signal log). BANG claimed four sunk and one damaged; REDFISH two sunk (her Attacks 1 and 3, 0104 and 0141 K); SHAD's one salvo, fired by mistake at a torpedo boat at 2338 K, missed. The postwar credit gives BANG Sakae and Amakusa Maru and REDFISH Hozan Maru, but W-15 logged Hozan Maru torpedoed at 2339 I (0039 K), 25 minutes before REDFISH first fired and seven minutes after BANG's Attack 1.
Keelung to Naha, sailed 22 November; ships and escorts from W-15's battle report. The convoy's own record: [[convoy:taka-206]].
Positions are each navigator's own dead reckoning; lines between them are straight. REDFISH's chronology position for Hozan Maru (24-27N 122-47E) is her own Attack 3 position, not the target's.

BANG, REDFISH and SHAD all kept zone K (−10) that night (the pack agreed "all times ... will be minus ten (King)"). Japanese records use Tokyo time (I, −9): Manazuru's red flare at 2240 I is 2340 K, 52 minutes before BANG's Attack 1.

REDFISH heard "first of many explosions; BANG apparently made her attack" at 0037 K and fired her own first torpedoes at 0104 K. W-15 saw Hozan Maru torpedoed at 2339 I (0039 K). By the reports' own clocks the hit fits BANG's attack, not REDFISH's; the US credit to REDFISH appears to rest on her Attack 1 or 3 claim.

War patrol reports, NARA microfilm M1752: BANG Patrol 4 (74802868), REDFISH Patrol 2 (74837267, 74837338), SHAD Patrol 8 (74848165). Minesweeper W-15's battle report on TAKA-206 via JACAR (C08030607900, National Institute for Defense Studies). Which ships sank, from combinedfleet.com, a secondary source, flagged where used. Coastline: Natural Earth.

outcome.note: SHAD fired three bow torpedoes at a CHIDORI-type torpedo boat at 800 yds at 2338 K (2238 I), all missed, and dived at 2340 K. Two minutes later the CHIDORI-class Manazuru fired a red flare for a surfaced submarine (J01, 2240 I); depth charges were heard at 2245 I (J02) against SHAD's close charges from 2343 K. No ship was lost until 2339 I. Manazuru survived the convoy (she sent the 1655 I order on the 23rd, p47)
The depth charges W-15 heard at 2245 I (2345 K) are the ones SHAD logged from 2343 K

The report names no damage from this attack: the first ship lost, Hozan Maru, was torpedoed at 2339 I, an hour later (BANG's Attack 1)

events.title: Attack 1
events.words: Torpedo attack No. 1 (times not zoned; King per narrative)

outcome.note: BANG fired at one medium AK at 2332 I from 2350 yds and saw it disappear; a ship was sunk at 2337 I 3.5 nm away (J03) and Hozan Maru was seen torpedoed at 2339 I (J02). The US Navy chronology gives Hozan Maru to REDFISH, and so does JANAC, as probable ("Submarine*"; janac:4/p76). REDFISH's report settles it for BANG: her first attack was at 0104 K (0004 I), 25 minutes after Hozan Maru was seen torpedoed, and W-15 named the ship sunk at 2337 I as Hozan Maru (J07). Attacks 1-3 were fired within three minutes; which of them hit is open

Of TAKA-206's six ships, three were sunk (Hozan, Amakusa, Sakae Maru) and three reached Funauki (J04). BANG claimed four sunk and one damaged in seven attacks; the postwar credit is two (Sakae, Amakusa; janac:6/p3), both marked "Submarine*", "*Probable Agent", as is Hozan Maru, credited to REDFISH (janac:4/p76)

The ship sunk at 2337 I (J03) was No. 2 ship Hozan Maru (J07). BANG's Attacks 1-3 (0032-0035 K = 2332-2335 I) are the only attacks on TAKA-206 in the minutes before; SHAD's had been an hour earlier and missed, REDFISH's first came at 0004 I. Probable rather than hit only because three of BANG's attacks share the window

The Navy's November summary has Hozan Maru sunk east of Formosa at 2337 I, five minutes after Attack 1 (2332 I), the same time as Manazuru's signal (J03), which it repeats; it adds no position. Probable for the same reason as J07: Attacks 1-3 share the window

events.title: Attack 2
events.words: Torpedo attack No. 2 (time 0032-50)

outcome.note: BANG claimed a large AK sunk ("2 Hits") at 0032-50 K, within a minute of Attack 1. The Japanese record has one ship sunk in those minutes, Hozan Maru (J03, J07), not two; Attacks 1, 2 and 3 all fit its time

Amakusa Maru and Sakae Maru, the other two ships lost, have no time or place in W-15's report: by 1655 I on the 23rd Sakae Maru was missing and Amakusa Maru unnamed (J04). Nor in the Navy's November summary (J09 names only Hozan Maru), and neither ship has a movement table in series 4 or 5, so no minutes or miles can be set against any attack. Any of BANG's claimed hits (Attacks 2, 3, 6, 7) or REDFISH's (her Attacks 1 and 3, 0006 and 0043 I) could be theirs; the postwar credit gives both to BANG (janac:6/p3), "probable agent"

events.note: The Navy's November 1944 day-by-day summary (escort and anti-submarine, 大東亜戦争経過概要), 22nd; the result is bracketed with the entry above it (1940, Dowa Maru, off Shinnanshoto). It is the only TAKA-206 loss in the summary: neither the 22nd nor the 23rd names Amakusa Maru or Sakae Maru. The tonnage, 2,345, is the figure W-15's convoy table (p33) sets against its No. 4 ship

events.note: W-15's log of the action, after Hozan Maru was torpedoed (J02). 2346 I = 0046 K, 0003-0005 I = 0103-0105 K. W-15 stayed behind to hunt and rescue (49 rescued by 0105 I, p41) and rejoined the convoy at 0120 I, so its log records nothing of BANG's later attacks. BANG was on the surface throughout; the contact was not BANG. One depth figure is unclear (?)

paras.text: Keelung to Naha, sailing at 0800 on 22 November 1944 with six ships and four escorts (W-15's battle report, p32–33). Three were sunk that night (Hozan, Amakusa and Sakae Maru); the other three sheltered at Funauki (Iriomote) on the 23rd. BANG, REDFISH and SHAD all attacked it (engagement `bang-patrol-4`).
**Cargo: not recorded** in W-15's report. The table gives each ship a type letter (A or C, not explained on the page), a top speed and a displacement.

It types two ranges (2600, 2750), two own speeds (8.5, 8.3) and two own courses (164 30, 161 30) one above the other, and one target course and speed. Attack 4 (tubes 1-3, at the ship) takes the first of each, Attack 5 (tubes 4-6, at the trailing escort) the second; the tracks agree with that pairing. The broaching remark covers all six torpedoes.

words.type_attack: NIGHT SURFACE ATTACK. Having obtained a favorable attack position on a CHIDORI escort, range 3,100 yards, 90 S track, gyro angle near 000, the bow tubes were ordered to be made ready. While oping the outer door of number 4 torpedo tube, a "hot run" in the tube followed, which jammed the gyro-spindle of that tube, thereby overloading the gyro-setter motor so that it failed to follow up thereafter. While matching gyro angles by hand, the forward torpedo room mistook a gyro angle for an order to fire and they did so. Three tubes were fired, none having match gyro angles.
words.target_line: TARGET DRAFT 6 Feet. COURSE 120 SPEED 6 RANGE 800 yards.
words.remarks: All three tubes were fired while attempting to match gyro angles by hand, and all were fired before being matched.
words.note: The typed tracks (120S for all three) are 7-9° from what own course 020 + the typed gyro angles (031, 032, 033) + 180 - target course 120 give (111S, 112S, 113S): kept as typed. The sheet says the gyros were being matched by hand when the tubes were fired and none had matched its gyro angle, so the typed gyro angles and the typed track need not agree. The type-attack paragraph gives the planned set-up as range 3,100 yards, 90 S track, gyro near 000, against the 800 yards and 120 S of the table. The sheet has no damage lines (no ship sunk or damaged is typed). A handwritten mark under the time (2338 K) is not read.
